newsitem.title: USA: Toys R Us posts strong Q2 amid higher sales.
newsitem.headline: Toys R Us posts strong Q2 amid higher sales.

text.p: Toys R Us Inc. on Monday reported higher second-quarter earnings, attributed to higher sales of video games and action figures, and lower interest expense.
The company earned $36.7 million, or 13 cents a share, in the quarter ended Aug. 2, easily beating Wall Street's consensus projection of 11 cents a share.
A year earlier, Toys R Us posted a loss of $7.5 million, or 3 cents per share, affected by a $55 million arbitration award against the company.

Current quarter sales increased 15 percent to $1.99 billion from $1.74 billion in 1996, while U.S. same-store sales -- sales by stores open at least a year -- rose 4 percent for the quarter. Same-store sales rose 6 percent in the first half.

"These sales gains are attributable to the continued strength of the video game business as well as strong sales of action figures, plush and outdoor play sets. In addition, the virtual pet craze spurred by Tamagotchi has further increased customer traffic in our stores," the company said in a statement.

The company said its Kids R Us childrens clothing division posted higher comparable sales for the quarter, but its Babies R Us same-store sales decreased. It added that stores in Canada and the United Kingdom posted double-digit same-store sales growth for the quarter and the first half.
Toys R Us said lower interest expense due to improved cash flow and expense control also contributed to its second-quarter earnings.
The company's stock was down 19 cents at $32.81 in composite morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
